intro: Two learning objectives may request opposing movements of shared parameters. Inspect their pairwise direction agreement.
task: Return cosine similarities and a boolean matrix identifying strictly negative cosine similarity.
requirements: gradients is tasks-by-parameters. Define cosine as zero whenever either row has zero norm.
Return {"cosine": square matrix, "conflict": boolean square matrix}. Nonzero rows have self-cosine one; zero rows have self-cosine zero.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Zero task
Same direction

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Normalize nonzero rows, then form their Gram matrix.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Opposite vectors conflict, while perpendicular and zero vectors do not.

explanation: A negative dot product means a step improving one linearized task can worsen the other. Cosine similarity removes magnitude to isolate this directional disagreement.
The audit is local to the supplied gradients. It does not modify them or establish long-term task incompatibility, and zero gradients have no defined direction under the chosen zero convention.
